title: The closed sidebar is a rail of tiles, and the bars show hover
body:
The closed sidebar is a 3-column strip with one state glyph per workspace, and nothing in the frame tracks the pointer, so no part of the top bar or sidebar shows a hover state. Board C of the mockup draws the closed sidebar as a rail of workspace tiles with a popover card.

## Proposal

- `CLOSED_WIDTH` goes to 5 columns. Each workspace is a rounded tile about 1.5 rows tall with its initial in bold, half a row apart, most urgent first. A dot in the state colour sits on the tile's top-right corner, ringed in the sidebar's colour, when an agent has reported. The current tile is filled with `SELECTION` and ringed in `ACCENT`. A last tile reads `+` with a plain outline.
- A click on a tile shows its workspace, and `+` starts a new one.
- The frame learns the pointer's position over the chrome, and decade redraws when the hovered item changes.
- Hovering a tile shows the workspace's card beside the rail, above the panes, on `LIGHTER_BACKGROUND` with a 1 px border, a darker rect offset a few pixels as its shadow, and a last line reading `click to show`. A hovered tile gets `LIGHTER_BACKGROUND` and a `LIGHT_FOREGROUND` ring.
- In the top bar, a hovered inactive tab pill fills with `SELECTION`, a hovered state pill takes a lighter tint, and a hovered `≡` brightens.
close_reason: Landed in b25d04d. `Frame::hover` and `State.frame_hover` track the hovered item, and `draw_above` draws the popover over the panes.
